 Learn more Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman, Pras Subramanian, and Jake Conley discuss reporting by Hunterbrook alleging AMD ( AMD ) kept supplying firmware updates to a U.S.-blacklisted Chinese server maker, raising export-control questions and causing its stock to sink. 
 Video Transcript 00:00 Speaker A and I want to mention what's going on with shares of AMD right now. They are um falling pretty sharply here. 
 00:10 Speaker A There is a report out from Hunterbrook, um which is um a a media outlet but that also makes has a hedge fund connected to it that makes short bets mostly tied to its reporting. 
 00:26 Speaker A and it looks like that they are reporting some similar things to what we were hearing about from Nvidia. Is that is that right? 
 00:32 Speaker B It's right. So they've put out a report. It just came just crossed the wire um just a few minutes ago, really, about 20 minutes ago. 
 00:41 Speaker B And what they're what they're, you know, setting up here with their research is that uh the US has blacklisted a Chinese server maker called IEIT systems. 
 00:51 Speaker B And uh what the report alleges and finds is that the the the company, that company that's blacklisted, kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run inside those servers, which could be seen as a contravention of US export control policy. 
 01:06 Speaker B Um they're also finding that three companies closely tied to IEIT, this this blacklisted company, use the same AMD firmware. 
 01:13 Speaker B So tying AMD to companies that have been targeted by the US government uh for some sort of problematic behavior. 
 01:23 Speaker B And the idea here would be that this is something that's going around export controls uh potentially illegally. 
 01:28 Speaker C So, so was AMD providing these, I guess BIOS updates to to uh to I E I T? 
 01:34 Speaker B IEIT. So what what Hunterbrook's alleging is that the comp- IEIT, this blacklisted company kept receiving new firmware, which then enabled AMD chips, getting that firmware from AMD. 
 01:46 Speaker B And that which enables AMD chips to be used in those servers continuously. The idea here would be that if the blacklist comes down on IEIT, The idea is that AMD should say, okay, we're done doing business. 
 01:55 Speaker C Yeah, yeah, yeah. But they kept 
 01:55 Speaker B But it sounds like they kept doing firmware updates, which meant that company could keep using their silicon. 
 01:58 Speaker C And I haven't read the report so I'm I'm curious if like this is just a clerical error or if it's actually, oh, we want to support these clients because they're spending a lot of money. 
 02:04 Speaker B We should note a very, very deep, long report. We're just going through the headlines here that they have a summary. 
 02:09 Speaker A And also we should know we haven't at this point had time to go out to AMD to ask on that report. So that's important to note as well. This is just breaking. 
 02:18 Speaker A So we're we're mentioning it as because we are seeing um the reaction in the shares. 
 02:22 Speaker B Hunter Hunterbrook mentioning that um 8.7%. Yeah, 9% down. Hunterbrook mentioning AMD did not answer their questions. 
 02:29 Speaker B Um we ourselves at Yahoo Finance have not had a chance to go out to AMD at this point.
